title: Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions
summary: Read, plot and transform points in four quadrants, then use coordinate differences to solve geometric problems.
objectives: Read and interpret ordered pairs in all four quadrants.
Use coordinates to describe translations, reflections and midpoints.
Find horizontal and vertical lengths, perimeters and areas from coordinates.

blocks.text: An ordered pair is written (x, y): move horizontally to x first, then vertically to y. The signs identify the quadrant. Points on the x-axis have y = 0, points on the y-axis have x = 0, and the origin is (0, 0).

A horizontal length is the absolute difference between x-coordinates; a vertical length is the absolute difference between y-coordinates. Reflection in the x-axis changes the sign of y, while reflection in the y-axis changes the sign of x.

sections.title: Rectangle from four coordinates

prompt.text: A rectangle has vertices (-3, 4), (5, 4), (5, -2) and (-3, -2). Find its perimeter.

sections.verification_note: The opposite sides have equal lengths, and 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28.

prompt.text: Point A(-4, 7) is reflected in the y-axis. State the x-coordinate of its image.

feedback.text: Reflection in the y-axis changes -4 to 4 and keeps the y-coordinate unchanged.

blocks.text: Read x before y, track signs carefully, and use coordinate differences for axis-aligned lengths.
